claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can initially exist as a single-phase, disordered high-temperature BCC solid solution.
The high-temperature BCC state is maintained by a modest thermodynamic driving force for ordering counterbalanced by strongly sluggish diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion kinetically traps Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 in a disordered BCC structure and postpones ordering or phase separation until lower temperatures.
Local chemical-order fluctuations and diffusion-mediated short-range clustering occur in the disordered BCC lattice.
High configurational entropy in the multicomponent alloy weakens the thermodynamic driving force for ordering.
Mixing enthalpies can be used to estimate the alloy's thermodynamic driving force for ordering.
High activation-energy barriers for atomic rearrangement cause very slow diffusion in this alloy.
Above approximately 1000 K, prolonged annealing will leave Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 as a single-phase disordered BCC solid solution.
Lower-temperature annealing will promote ordered domains, potentially B2, and eventual phase decomposition.
The degree of ordering will increase as annealing temperature decreases.
The degree of ordering will increase with dwell time.
Rapidly quenched Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a homogeneous BCC structure.
Changing the Cr/Co balance changes ordering, decomposition, and phase-stability tendencies in Al-containing Cr-Co-Fe-Ni alloys.
In related Al-Co-Fe-Ni alloys, replacing part of the Co with Cr and lowering the annealing temperature promotes decomposition into ordered B2 and disordered BCC phases.
Related AlxCrCoFeNi alloys exhibit chemical clustering over a broad temperature range for x below 0.5 and show high-temperature short-range ordering.
The proposed kinetic-trapping mechanism would be falsified if annealing above approximately 1000 K produces significant B2 ordering or phase decomposition.
